provenance: Hand-authored reader-facing wording for the four categories already published in prompt-literacy-rubric.json. Contains no provider, HRIS, customer or telemetry data, no prompt text, and no department name.
weightRule: NO WEIGHT IS WRITTEN DOWN IN THIS FILE. Each entry names the rubric category it is the reader-facing form of, and the number it contributes is read from prompt-literacy-rubric.json through categoryScoreWeight(). A reader-facing label therefore cannot carry a weight the published rubric does not, and a rubric change moves this control without an edit here.
assumptionRule: Every entry states, in one line, why the rubric weight it inherits is the right one for the workload it describes. An entry without a non-empty assumption is a weight nobody can defend, and tests/reader-classified-grade.test.js fails on it.
orderingRule: Listed best-scoring first, so the picker reads as a scale rather than as an unordered menu. The order is presentation only; it is not read by the arithmetic.
unclassifiedRule: There is deliberately no 'mixed' or 'not sure' entry. A department the reader has not classified is counted as unclassified spend and named in the shortfall sentence, because a middling weight assigned to a department nobody looked at would move a published letter with no evidence behind it.

categories.label: Mostly structured delivery work — context, constraints, and what a correct answer looks like
categories.assumption: Full marks, because this is the rubric's own definition of its reference class rather than a claim that the department is faultless. A reader picking it is asserting the same thing the rubric asserts about a high-value prompt: the request carried its context, it was answered in one pass, and the model was matched to the work.

categories.label: Mostly simple tasks — formatting, renaming, boilerplate — on the most expensive model available
categories.assumption: Keeps most of the intent and efficiency credit and none of the model-fit credit, because the work is legitimate and arrives in one pass; what went wrong is a routing decision a gateway rule can correct without the requester changing anything.

categories.label: Mostly repeated attempts — the same question re-asked until something usable comes back
categories.assumption: Scores at the efficiency floor and keeps half of intent and model fit, because the goal was real and the model was not the mistake; a chain that had to repeat is evidence the first request omitted its failing state, and that is a coaching gap rather than a platform one.

categories.label: Mostly non-business use — personal, exploratory, or outside this team's work
categories.assumption: Earns no credit on any axis, because partial credit here would let leakage raise a department's letter, which is the one result an executive reading this number would call a lie.
